newsitem.title: USA: Lilly says may write-down PCS unit value.
newsitem.headline: Lilly says may write-down PCS unit value.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said Thursday it may have to write down the carrying value of its PCS Health Systems unit, which it acquired for $4.1 billion in 1994.

"As we update our cash-flow estimates, it may be necessary to reduce the current carrying value of PCS to fair-market value ... Regardless of that value, Lilly remains dedicated to continuing to grow PCS," said Lilly spokesman Edward West.
He said PCS' ability to increase profits has been hampered by intense competition and Lilly's inability to find an equity partner for the business.
"All of those facts compel us to continue to review the value of that asset," West told Reuters.

Indianapolis-based Lilly earlier Thursday said it agreed to sell its 40-percent stake in Dow Elanco, an agricultural chemicals joint venture with Dow Chemical Co, for $1.2 billion, including $300 million in undistributed earnings.
Dow agreed to buy the stake, making the Midland, Mich.-based chemicals giant the sole owner of Dow Elanco.
Wall Street analysts had long expected a Dow Elanco sale by Lilly to be followed by a PCS asset write-down.
"It's likely we will hear something about PCS in this quarter and it should be a write-down of some kind," said Merrill Lynch drug industry analyst Richard Vietor.

Lilly said it expected to record a one-time, after-tax gain on the Dow Elanco sale of $310 million to $340 million. It said earnings for the second quarter may get a boost from the gain in the range of $0.56 to $0.62 per share.
That gain likely will be used to offset any damage to the company's results that could come from a PCS write-down, analysts said.
"There's earnings management going on here," Vietor said.
